entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
1. Petitioner has filed this miscellaneous bail application under Section 438 Cr.P.C.
2. F.I.R. No.218/2017 was registered at Police Station Kaman, District Bharatpur for offence under Sections 420, 272 of I.P.C. and Sections 58, 59 of Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006.

3. It is contended by counsel for the petitioner that offences under Sections 58, 59 of Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006 as well as offences under Sections 272 of IPC are bailable and Section 420 of IPC has been added to make it a non-bailable offence.
4.
Learned Public Prosecutor has opposed the bail application.
6. Considering the contentions put forth by counsel for the petitioner, I deem it proper to allow the anticipatory bail (2 of 2) [CRLMB-12091/2017] application.
7. The anticipatory bail application is allowed.

The S.H.O/I.O/Arresting Officer, Police Station Kaman, District Bharatpur in F.I.R. No. 218/2017 is directed that in the event of arrest of the petitioner he shall be released on bail, provided he furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties in the sum of Rs. 25,000/- each to his satisfaction on the following Aas Khan@Aas Mohammad vs State Of Rajasthan Through Pp on 3 January, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187371807/
1 conditions :-
(i). that the petitioner shall make himself available for interrogation by a police officer as and when required;
(ii). that the petitioner shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the court or any police officer, and (iii). that the petitioner shall not leave India without previous permission of the court.
